title: What Computer Vision Can Do · Level 2
slo: Identify the computer vision technique that fits a simple workplace image task.

exercises.question_text: Image classification identifies several objects and gives each one a rectangular location.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A checkout image with many items would be matched to the wrong kind of result.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Image classification predicts one main-subject label. Object detection finds multiple objects and bounding boxes.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Several objects plus rectangular locations describe object detection.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence no longer clearly shows what information is combined and why.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the model, then join images with text, and finish with the visual-language purpose.

exercises.correct_answer: A multimodal model combines images with text to link visual language
exercises.explanation: The defining feature is combining image and text information. That combination supports relationships between visual content and language.

exercises.question_text: A grocery checkout clerk places one fruit at a time on a camera-connected scale. The system must identify its type to charge by weight. Which actions fit image classification? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Correctly named fruit images are used to train image classification.
Correct. The result can be one fruit-type label for the item.

options.text: Use the predicted type for pricing
options.rationale: Correct. The identified produce type can be used with weight to charge the amount.

options.text: Draw a box around every item
options.error_type: confuses one-item classification with object detection
options.rationale: Not quite. The task has one fruit at a time and needs its type, not locations for many items.
options.better_fit: Choose this when one image contains several items that must each be located.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk would get rectangles even though the important result is the fruit type.
feedback.instructional: One main item and one type label fit image classification. Boxes are used by object detection.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Labeled fruit images support a one-item type prediction, which can guide pricing by weight.

exercises.question_text: A retail manager wants a system to use a product photo and its written description together. Which choices fit a multimodal model? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. The product photo contributes image information.
Correct. The written description contributes text information.
Correct. Combining the photo and description supports visual-language relationships.

options.error_type: confuses multimodal processing with object detection
options.rationale: Not quite. Using only image regions leaves out the written description and is not multimodal.
options.better_fit: Choose this when the task is to examine image areas for possible objects.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager's written product description would not be used with the photo.
feedback.instructional: A multimodal model combines image and text information. Examining image regions is associated with object detection.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The photo and written description are two modalities that can be combined to link visual content with language.

exercises.question_text: In object detection, the coordinate-defined rectangle around a found object is a ___.

parts.text: In object detection, the coordinate-defined rectangle around a found object is a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The object's location would not be named with the correct kind of marker.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use bounding box for the coordinate-defined rectangle. Image classification predicts one label, while semantic segmentation classifies pixels.

exercises.explanation: Object detection reports where an object appears with a rectangle defined by coordinates. Image classification and semantic segmentation name different tasks, not this rectangle.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence no longer clearly links pixels to the objects they form.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the technique first, then state that each pixel is classified by the object it belongs to.

exercises.correct_answer: Semantic segmentation classifies each pixel by the object it belongs to
exercises.explanation: The defining action is assigning individual pixels according to their object. This creates a precise location result.

exercises.question_text: A grocery-store manager needs a checkout camera to find a cereal box, a bottle, and an apple in one image, including where each item appears. Which technique fits?

options.rationale: Correct. The image contains multiple items, and the task needs each item's location.

options.error_type: confuses one main-subject label with multiple objects
options.rationale: Not quite. Image classification predicts one label for the main subject of an image.
options.better_fit: Choose this when one item is shown and only its type is needed.

feedback.intrinsic: The checkout could receive one label instead of locations for all three items.
feedback.instructional: Multiple individual objects and their locations require object detection.

options.error_type: chooses pixel-level precision when boxes are requested
options.rationale: Not quite. Semantic segmentation gives pixel-level location, while this task asks where items appear.
options.better_fit: Choose this when exact pixels or an exact item outline are required.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager could get more location detail than the rectangular areas needed.
feedback.instructional: Object detection uses rectangular bounding boxes. Semantic segmentation classifies individual pixels.

options.error_type: confuses object locations with image interpretation
options.rationale: Not quite. Contextual image analysis can describe a scene but does not provide the stated location result.
options.better_fit: Choose this when the camera image needs a description or relevant tags.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager might get a scene description without each item's location.
feedback.instructional: Descriptions concern contextual image analysis. Object detection identifies objects and where they appear.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Multiple items plus where each appears is the purpose of object detection.

exercises.question_text: The AI field that processes images, videos, and live camera streams is ___.

parts.text: The AI field that processes images, videos, and live camera streams is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The answer names only part of the work done with visual input.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use computer vision for the broad area. Image classification predicts one label, while contextual image analysis interprets image-and-text relationships.

exercises.explanation: This name covers processing visual input in several forms. Image classification and contextual image analysis are narrower tasks within that area.

exercises.question_text: A safety manager reviews a camera image and needs the exact pixels that belong to each worker. Which choices fit semantic segmentation? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Semantic segmentation makes a classification for each individual pixel.
Correct. Pixels can be classified by the worker they belong to.
Correct. Pixel-level classification gives a precise object location.

options.text: Predict one label for the whole image
options.error_type: confuses semantic segmentation with image classification
options.rationale: Not quite. One label for the image does not identify the exact pixels of each worker.
options.better_fit: Choose this when one main subject needs one overall label.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager would not receive the exact worker pixels needed for the review.
feedback.instructional: Exact object pixels call for semantic segmentation. A whole-image label is image classification.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The request for exact worker pixels matches pixel-level classification.

exercises.question_text: Models that connect image objects with descriptive text can perform ___.

parts.text: Models that connect image objects with descriptive text can perform

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The image could be given only a label or a model category instead of the requested interpretation task.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use contextual image analysis for interpreting image-and-text relationships. Image classification predicts one label; a multimodal model combines information types.

exercises.explanation: Connecting visual objects with descriptive text enables scene interpretation, descriptions, and relevant tags. Image classification gives one label, while multimodal model names the model type that can combine modalities.

exercises.question_text: A homeowner's doorbell camera sends a live feed to a security app. The app must process the feed to detect people. Which AI area should the developer use?

options.rationale: Correct. The task processes a live camera feed, which is visual input.

options.error_type: chooses one specific vision task instead of the broader AI area
options.rationale: Not quite. Image classification predicts one main-subject label, while the question asks for the broader area.
options.better_fit: Choose this when a single image needs one label for its main subject.

feedback.intrinsic: The doorbell task could be described too narrowly before deciding what result is needed.
feedback.instructional: Processing a live feed belongs to computer vision. Image classification is one possible technique within it.

options.rationale: Not quite. Contextual image analysis is for interpreting scenes and generating descriptions or tags.
options.better_fit: Choose this when a photo needs a description of objects and activities.

feedback.intrinsic: The homeowner might receive descriptions when the immediate need is detecting people.
feedback.instructional: Contextual image analysis connects visual content with language. The broader live-feed work is computer vision.

options.error_type: confuses a model type with the broad AI area
options.rationale: Not quite. A multimodal model combines more than one kind of information, such as images and text.
options.better_fit: Choose this when the camera content must be connected with written language.

feedback.intrinsic: The task could add text processing even though only visual input is stated.
feedback.instructional: Multimodal models combine modalities. Computer vision is the area for processing the camera feed.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A live doorbell feed is visual input, so this belongs to computer vision.

exercises.question_text: A communications manager uploads an event photo and needs a sentence describing the objects and activities shown. Which technique should the manager use?

options.rationale: Correct. The requested sentence describes objects and activities shown in the photo.

options.error_type: chooses one label instead of a scene description
options.rationale: Not quite. Image classification provides one main-subject label, not a sentence about a scene.
options.better_fit: Choose this when the manager needs one label for the photo's main subject.

feedback.intrinsic: The event photo could receive only one name instead of the requested description.
feedback.instructional: A scene description requires interpreting objects and activities, which is contextual image analysis.

options.error_type: chooses object locations instead of activity interpretation
options.rationale: Not quite. Object detection finds objects and locations, but the request is for a sentence about activities.
options.better_fit: Choose this when the manager needs each object and where it appears.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager could receive rectangles around objects but no description of the event.
feedback.instructional: Bounding-box locations are object detection results. Contextual image analysis interprets activities and generates descriptions.

options.error_type: chooses pixel classification instead of a description
options.rationale: Not quite. Semantic segmentation assigns individual pixels to objects, not a written scene description.
options.better_fit: Choose this when exact object pixels or outlines are needed.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager could get outlines without the sentence needed for communication.
feedback.instructional: Pixel-level location is semantic segmentation. Contextual image analysis connects visual content with language.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A description of objects and activities is a contextual image analysis task.
